text:
runtime-bot: ALERT: Canary rollout model-x:v3 -> p99 latency +120% vs v2 over last 15m. Affected region: us-west-2. Related traces: https://internal.traces/redwood/abc123 :warning:

zoe: seeing the same in Grafana, p50 up ~30ms, p99 jumping a lot. Canary is 10% traffic. Rolling back? :thinking:

akshay: quick snapshot from cpu/gpu profiler on one affected host:
```
# profiler summary (canary pod 7):
- total tokens served: 42k
- avg seq_len: 78 -> baseline 44
- kernel_time breakdown:
  fused_attention_fast: 18%
  matmul_generic_slow: 46%  <-- increased
  kv_cache_ops: 12%
  other: 24%
- observed kernel selection: many calls falling back to matmul_generic_slow at seq_len 64-128 boundary
```

marta: interesting — model-x:v3 changed tokenizer whitespace normalization, we saw avg seq_len increase in unit tests but thought it was minor. Could that push kernels into different tiling paths?

jinsung: also KV cache hit rate dropped on canary: 0.55 vs 0.82 baseline (15m). Looks like prefix reuse is much lower, so more KV writes/reads and less reuse. Might explain extra kernel calls + memory churn.

zoe: so two hypotheses: (1) seq-len distribution shifted triggering fallback kernels that are slower on our current CUDA kernels, (2) KV cache churn + eviction causing extra memcpy overhead / kernel warm-ups. Either could raise p99.

akshay: I pulled the kernel selection log (sanitized):
```
[2026-03-05T10:12:03Z] seq_len=60 -> selected fused_attention_fast
[2026-03-05T10:12:03Z] seq_len=65 -> attempted fused_attention_fast -> fallback matmul_generic_slow (heuristic mismatch)
[2026-03-05T10:12:04Z] seq_len=120 -> selected matmul_generic_slow
```
Note the heuristic uses bucket thresholds + measured warmup latency. The tokenizer pushes many requests just above the fast path threshold.

marta: we recently shipped a kernel compile tweak that removed a smaller-block specialized kernel for fp16 to simplify maintenance (PR 5421). Could be compounding. The fallback path is generic but slower.

benchbot: I ran a micro-bench on a canary-box with synthetic seq length mix (samples attached) and saw p99 delta ~1.9x when 30% of requests are in 64-96 range. Raw numbers:
```
baseline mix -> p99 88ms
v3 mix     -> p99 165ms
```

jinsung: KV cache logs (snippet):
```
cache_hits=0.56 cache_misses=0.44 evictions=120/s mem_copy_bytes=12MB/s
```
Evictions spike correlates with request bursts. Looks like tokenizer changed token boundaries so prefixes don't align with previous cache keys as often.

zoe: actionable options? immediate: rollback v3 canary to v2 and disable auto-rollout. Medium-term: add a canary perf gate that checks seq_len distribution + kv cache hit rate and kernel selection histograms. Also consider restoring the specialized small-block kernel or adjust boundaries.

akshay: agree. Quick mitigation we can try without rollback: force kernel selection override for canary pods to prefer fused_attention_fast up to seq_len=96 (override flag). That should reduce p99 while we debug. I'll test an override on a single canary slice.

marta: I'll open PR to re-introduce the small-block fp16 kernel variant behind a feature flag so we can A/B test. Also adding a telemetry metric: kernel_fallback_count per model-version.

jinsung: I'll prepare a KV cache warmup shim for canary that primes common prefixes from training set to bump hit-rate during rollout. Not a permanent fix but useful for ramp.

zoe: owners: akshay -> test kernel override (30m), jinsung -> kv warmup script (1h), marta -> PR for kernel variant + perf gate (EOD). I'll hold rollback if akshay's override shows good p99 improvement.

runtime-bot: Incident ticket created: INF-2026-1873. Linking thread. :white_check_mark:

zoe: thanks team. Also let's add a postmortem checklist item: include tokenizer changes in rollout perf tests (seq_len histogram + kv cache sim).

akshay: update: kernel override on canary slice applied, waiting for metric window (10m).

benchbot: 6m after override -> p99 dropped from 165ms to 96ms on that slice, kv hit-rate unchanged (~0.57). Seems kernel path change is main driver for p99.

zoe: great, hold rollout and coordinate with marta for the kernel PR + perf gate. We'll keep INF-2026-1873 open and follow up with a short postmortem after fix. :thumbsup:
